title: ‘Nightmare fodder’: Roku’s AI slop channel is even worse than expected
excerpt: Fairground TV is a 24/7 channel devoted to low-quality AI content for viewers sick of watching real people move in ways that won’t haunt you
content_html:
The appeal of Roku is that, whatever you happen to want to watch, there will almost certainly be a live channel for it. Just want to watch Little House on the Prairie? There’s a channel for it. Just want to watch Duck Dynasty? There’s a channel for that too. Purely want to watch nothing but local news from Wisconsin? Guess what: there’s a channel for that too.

But despite this wealth, a section of the population was still to see its needs fulfilled. What about people who hate plot and vision and the sight of people speaking convincing dialogue that synchronises perfectly with the movement of their lips? What about the people who just want to watch an unyielding torrent of eerily weightless nightmare fodder? Well, good news. Roku has finally caught up.

It was reported last week that Roku launched the Fairground AI Creator TV channel, the first free, all-AI streaming channel that pulls content from roughly 100 AI creators around the world. Early reactions were, to put it mildly, not great. The Verge compared it to eating from a trough, while Futurism called it “bottom-of-the-barrel slop”.

In truth, you will not watch Fairground AI Creator TV, and that’s sort of the point. This is television with vanishingly low production costs. Compare an hour of this cheap slop with, say, the tens of millions of dollars it takes to produce an episode of Stranger Things, and you’ll soon understand why executives might find the prospect irresistible. In this landscape you don’t need breakout hits, just enough stoned and curious students at 3am to turn a profit.

That said, I have actually just spent a few hours watching Fairground AI Creator TV, more out of self-hatred than anything else, and it would appear that the early reviews are right. On the plus side, the channel is evidence that artificial intelligence has come on in leaps and bounds over the last couple of years. Had this been attempted in 2023, we would have had a 24/7 feed of mutant Will Smith choking down handfuls of writhing spaghetti, and everyone would have vomited themselves dry. Generally speaking, what Fairground has to offer is much better.

However, it is still awful. Categorically, catastrophically awful. The channel doesn’t so much offer shows as a drifting dreamscape of bad ideas rendered as horribly as possible with no thought paid to scheduling. At one point on Wednesday, a shrill high-frequency anime gave way to a long and staid German-language short about Nazi bureaucracy. After that came a sort of Gladiator ripoff that had all the dynamism of an exhibit you’d see at the fourth-best museum on a poorly planned family holiday.

In fact, as an aside, there seems to be an awful lot of this. Switch on Fairground at any time of day and I’d estimate you are no more than 15 minutes away from seeing a witless, sepia historical drama of some description, full of craggy, burly men glowering at each other, dramatically lit by sunset regardless of which direction they’re facing. There is so much of it that it worries me about the future of the medium. The promise of AI is that it allows limitless story potential, and yet the bulk of it ends up looking like what would happen if your dad lucked himself a job scheduling Sunday afternoons on ITV3.

There are still horrible glitches to navigate – stray mouths that don’t move in time with dialogue, impossible physics, one specific instance of a man trudging through snow while his feet bizarrely made a clip-cloppy hoof noise – but these are becoming less and less frequent as the technology improves. The bad news about this is that you’re forced to concentrate on the storytelling ability of the people who made this. And you simply cannot.

Because it – all of it, every last stinking second of every godawful film – is completely inert. It is devoid of weight, of life, of vision and wit. The channel just flatly sits there, impressed by itself despite being physically unable to hold anybody’s attention. You may as well be watching a screensaver, a CD-Rom menu screen or a fridge.

The hope is obviously that something like Fairground will be the future of entertainment, churning out muck for pennies while an entire stratum of creatives go hungry. And who knows, one day it might achieve this. The technology is moving so quickly that it isn’t impossible to see it eventually developing the capacity to convincingly entertain.

But on the basis of what I’ve seen, that day is still a long way off. At one point, the channel cut away to a commercial for Roku’s Dr Phil channel, and the sight of an actual flesh-and-blood human acting in an identifiably human way almost moved me to tears. And surely anything that makes you emotional about Dr Phil of all people doesn’t deserve to exist.

content_html_zh:
Roku 的吸引力在于，无论你想看什么，几乎肯定会有一个直播频道。 只想看草原小屋？ 有一个渠道。 只想看《鸭子王朝》？ 也有一个渠道。 只想看威斯康星州当地新闻？ 你猜怎么着：也有一个渠道。

但尽管有这些财富，仍有一部分人的需求需要得到满足。 那些讨厌情节和视觉以及讨厌人们说出令人信服的对话且与嘴唇的动作完美同步的人呢？ 那些只想观看一股不屈不挠的怪异失重噩梦素材的人呢？ 嗯，好消息。 Roku终于追上了。

据报道，上周 Roku 推出了 Fairground AI Creator TV 频道，这是第一个免费的全 AI 流媒体频道，从全球大约 100 位 AI 创作者那里获取内容。 温和地说，早期的反应并不好。 The Verge 将其比作从槽中进食，而未来主义则将其称为“桶底污水”。

事实上，你不会看 Fairground AI Creator TV，这就是重点。 这是制作成本极低的电视。 将一小时的廉价内容与制作一集《怪奇物语》所需的数千万美元进行比较，你很快就会明白为什么高管们可能会发现这种前景不可抗拒。 在这种情况下，你不需要突破性的点击，只需要凌晨 3 点足够多的醉酒和好奇的学生就可以盈利。

也就是说，我实际上只是花了几个小时观看 Fairground AI Creator TV，更多的是出于自我憎恨而不是其他任何原因，看来早期的评论是正确的。 从好的方面来看，该渠道证明人工智能在过去几年中取得了突飞猛进的发展。 如果在 2023 年尝试这样做，我们就会看到变种人威尔·史密斯 (Will Smith) 24/7 不间断地吞下一把翻腾的意大利面，每个人都会把自己吐干。 总的来说，Fairground 提供的东西要好得多。

然而，它仍然很糟糕。 绝对是灾难性的可怕。 该频道提供的节目与其说是一个飘忽不定的糟糕想法的梦境，不如说是在不考虑时间安排的情况下尽可能可怕地呈现出来的。 周三，一部刺耳的高频动画被一部关于纳粹官僚机构的长而古板的德语短片所取代。 在那之后，出现了一种模仿角斗士的作品，它具有你在计划不周的家庭假期中在第四好的博物馆中看到的展览的所有活力。

事实上，顺便说一句，这样的事情似乎有很多。 在一天中的任何时候打开 Fairground，我估计你不到 15 分钟就会看到一场愚蠢的、深褐色的历史剧，里面充满了粗犷、魁梧的男人互相怒视，无论他们面向哪个方向，都被日落戏剧性地照亮。 如此之多，让我对媒体的未来感到担忧。 人工智能的承诺是它可以提供无限的故事潜力，但其中大部分内容最终看起来就像是如果你的父亲幸运地找到了一份安排周日下午在 ITV3 上播出的工作，将会发生什么。

仍然存在一些可怕的小故障需要导航——与对话不及时移动的嘴巴、不可能的物理原理、一个人在雪地里艰难跋涉而他的脚奇怪地发出马蹄声的具体例子——但随着技术的进步，这些问题正变得越来越少。 坏消息是你被迫专注于制作这个的人讲故事的能力。 而你根本做不到。

因为它——所有的一切，每部糟糕电影的最后一秒——都是完全惰性的。 它没有重量、没有生命、没有远见、没有智慧。 尽管无法吸引任何人的注意力，但该频道只是静静地坐在那里，对自己印象深刻。 您可能还正在观看屏幕保护程序、CD-ROM 菜单屏幕或冰箱。

显然，人们希望像 Fairground 这样的东西能够成为娱乐业的未来，在整个创意阶层都在挨饿的情况下，为几便士而生产垃圾。 谁知道，有一天它可能会实现这一目标。 这项技术发展得如此之快，以至于它最终发展出令人信服的娱乐能力并非不可能。

但从我所看到的情况来看，那一天还很遥远。 有一次，频道切到了 Roku 菲尔博士频道的广告，看到一个有血有肉的人以明显的人类方式行事，我几乎感动得流下了眼泪。 当然，任何让你对菲尔博士产生感情的事情都不值得存在。
